# Iris component library

<!-- Generated by tools/build_skill_refs.py from catalog/v1.library.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

This is the component library for the iris_ui tool. Pass the program as the `code` argument; your reply itself stays ordinary text, and `fallback` carries the same content as Markdown. The rules below describe the language the program is written in.

## Syntax Rules

1. Each statement is on its own line: `identifier = Expression`
2. `root` is the entry point — every program must define `root = Stack(...)`
3. Expressions are: strings ("..."), numbers, booleans (true/false), null, arrays ([...]), objects ({...}), or component calls TypeName(arg1, arg2, ...)
4. Use references for readability: define `name = ...` on one line, then use `name` later
5. EVERY variable (except root) MUST be referenced by at least one other variable. Unreferenced variables are silently dropped and will NOT render. Always include defined variables in their parent's children/items array.
6. Arguments are POSITIONAL (order matters, not names). Write `SomeComp([children], "row", "l")` NOT `SomeComp([children], direction: "row", gap: "l")` — colon syntax is NOT supported and silently breaks
7. Optional arguments can be omitted from the end
8. Declare mutable state with `$varName = defaultValue`. Components marked with `$binding` can read/write these. Undeclared $variables are auto-created with null default.
9. String concatenation: `"text" + $var + "more"`
10. Dot member access: `query.field` reads a field; on arrays it extracts that field from every element
11. Index access: `arr[0]`, `data[index]`
12. Arithmetic operators: +, -, *, /, % (work on numbers; + is string concat when either side is a string)
13. Comparison: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=
14. Logical: &&, ||, ! (prefix)
15. Ternary: `condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse`
16. Parentheses for grouping: `(a + b) * c`
- Strings use double quotes with backslash escaping

## Component Signatures

Arguments marked with ? are optional. Sub-components can be inline or referenced; prefer references for better streaming.
Props typed `ActionExpression` accept one @step, or Action([@steps...]) for several. See the Action section for available steps (@ToAssistant, @OpenUrl, @Set, @Reset, @Ask).
Props marked `$binding<type>` accept a `$variable` reference for two-way binding.

### Layout
Stack(children: any[], direction?: "column" | "row", gap?: "s" | "m" | "l") — Lays out children in a column (default) or a row. Use it as the root of almost every display
Card(children: any[], title?: string) — A bordered container with an optional title. One card per idea; do not nest cards
Section(title: string, children: any[]) — A heading followed by content, for grouping without a border
Divider() — A thin line between groups. Prefer Section to a bare divider
Tabs(items: Tab[]) — Switches between Tab children, one visible at a time. Keep to 2 to 5 tabs
Tab(label: string, children: any[]) — One page of a Tabs; the label is the tab title and should be a word or two
Expander(title: string, children: any[], open?: boolean) — A title that opens to reveal children; use for detail most people will not need

### Text and data
Text(value: string, variant?: "body" | "title" | "caption" | "mono") — A run of text; title is a heading, caption is small and muted, mono is for ids and paths
Markdown(value: string) — Formatted text (bold, lists, links, code); use when the content is already Markdown
KeyValue(key: string, value: string) — A label with its value on one line, for facts such as "Region: eu-west"
Stat(label: string, value: string, delta?: string, trend?: "up" | "down" | "flat") — One big number with a label and an optional change; keep value short, such as "12" or "98%"
StatRow(stats: Stat[]) — A row of 2 to 4 Stat components that share the width
StatusPill(label: string, tone?: "neutral" | "good" | "warn" | "bad") — A small coloured status label; tone says how it feels, so pick it for meaning, not looks
Table(columns: string[], rows: any[][]) — A grid of text. columns are the headings; each row has one cell per column. Up to about 6 columns
ListRow(title: string, subtitle?: string, trailing?: string) — A row with a title, an optional second line and trailing text, for lists of things
Timeline(items: TimelineItem[]) — Events in time order, oldest first, joined by a line
TimelineItem(title: string, time?: string, detail?: string) — One event on a Timeline; time is shown as given, so write it the way a person would say it
Checklist(items: ChecklistItem[]) — A read-only list of items that are done or not yet done
ChecklistItem(label: string, done?: boolean) — One line of a Checklist; done defaults to false
Progress(value: number, label?: string, style?: "bar" | "ring") — A bar (or ring) showing a value from 0 to 100, not a fraction
CodeBlock(code: string, language?: string) — Monospaced code with copy; language is a short name such as "dart" or "bash"
Diff(before: string, after: string) — Two versions of some text, with the changed lines marked. Use for edits, not for general comparison
Image(url: string, alt: string) — A picture from an allowed image host. alt is required and should describe it for a screen reader
Link(label: string, url: string) — Text that opens a web address after the person confirms. Use for sources, not for actions

### Charts
Sparkline(values: number[]) — A small trend line with no axes, for a quick sense of direction. Use LineChart when the person needs to read values
Series(name: string, values: number[]) — One named run of numbers in a LineChart or BarChart; keep the name short, it labels the legend
LineChart(series: Series[], labels?: string[]) — One to four Series as lines over shared labels, such as days. Every Series needs the same number of values as labels
BarChart(series: Series[], labels?: string[]) — One to four Series as grouped bars over shared labels. The baseline is zero, so use it to compare amounts, not to show a trend
Donut(slices: Slice[]) — Shares of a whole, up to 12 Slice values, shown as a ring with a legend. Use for parts of a total, not for trends
Slice(label: string, value: number) — One share of a Donut; value is any positive amount and the percentage is worked out for you

### Inputs
ChoiceChips(options: string[], value?: $binding<any>, multi?: boolean, label?: string) — A row of options to pick from. value is the chosen option, or with multi the list of chosen options. Use for a few short choices
Input(label: string, value?: $binding<string>, placeholder?: string, kind?: "text" | "number" | "multiline") — A text field. kind "number" stores a number, "multiline" gives room for a paragraph
Slider(label: string, min: number, max: number, value?: $binding<number>, step?: number) — Pick a number between min and max by dragging. step makes it move in whole steps. Use when the exact value matters less than the rough amount
Toggle(label: string, value?: $binding<boolean>) — An on/off switch with a label. value is true or false
DatePicker(label: string, value?: $binding<string>) — Pick a calendar date. value is written as text like "2026-11-07"
Stepper(label: string, value?: $binding<number>, min?: number, max?: number, step?: number) — A number with minus and plus buttons, for small counts such as guests or retries
ApproveReject(approveLabel: string, rejectLabel: string, askLabel?: string) — Two buttons for a yes-or-no decision, plus an optional third for asking first. Each sends its own label as the reply, so write each label as a sentence the person would say

### Actions
Button(label: string, action?: ActionExpression, variant?: "primary" | "secondary") — A button. Without an action it sends its label to the assistant as the person's next message
Submit(label: string, action: ActionExpression) — The primary button that ends a form. Its action runs with the values the person has entered, e.g. @Ask("Here is my answer", {choice: $choice})

## Built-in Functions

Data functions prefixed with `@` to distinguish from components. These are the ONLY functions available — do NOT invent new ones.
Use @-prefixed built-in functions (@Count, @Sum, @Avg, @Min, @Max, @Round) on data. Do NOT hardcode computed values.

@Count(array: any[]) → number — Returns array length
@First(array: any[]) → any — Returns first element of array
@Last(array: any[]) → any — Returns last element of array
@Sum(numbers: number[]) → number — Sum of numeric array
@Avg(numbers: number[]) → number — Average of numeric array
@Min(numbers: number[]) → number — Minimum value in array
@Max(numbers: number[]) → number — Maximum value in array
@Sort(array: any[], field: string, direction?: "asc" | "desc") → any[] — Sort array by field. Direction: "asc" (default) or "desc"
@Filter(array: any[], field: string, operator: "==" | "!=" | ">" | "<" | ">=" | "<=" | "contains", value: any) → any[] — Filter array by field value
@Round(number: number | number[], decimals?: number) → number | number[] — Round to N decimal places (default 0)
@Abs(number: number | number[]) → number | number[] — Absolute value
@Floor(number: number | number[]) → number | number[] — Round down to nearest integer
@Ceil(number: number | number[]) → number | number[] — Round up to nearest integer
@Each(array: any[], varName: string, template: any) — Evaluate template for each element. varName is the loop variable — use it ONLY inside the template expression (inline). Do NOT create a separate statement for the template.
@Percent(done: number, total: number) → number — done as a percentage of total, rounded to a whole number
@Money(value: number, currency: string) → string — value formatted as money in the given ISO currency code, such as "GBP"
@Ago(timestamp: any) → string — a timestamp (ISO 8601 text or epoch milliseconds) as relative time, such as "3 hours ago"

Builtins compose — output of one is input to the next:
`@Count(@Filter(data.rows, "field", "==", "val"))` for KPIs/chart values, `@Round(@Avg(data.rows.score), 1)`, `@Each(data.rows, "item", Comp(item.field))` for per-item rendering.
Array pluck: `data.rows.field` extracts a field from every row → use with @Sum, @Avg, charts, tables.

IMPORTANT @Each rule: The loop variable (e.g. "item") is ONLY available inside the @Each template expression. Always inline the template — do NOT extract it to a separate statement.
CORRECT: `list = @Each(rows, "t", Comp(t.name))`
WRONG: `item = Comp(t.name)` then `list = @Each(rows, "t", item)`, because t is undefined in item.

## Action — Button Behavior

An action wires a button click to operations. Pass one @-prefixed step bare, e.g. Button("Ask", @ToAssistant("Tell me more")). Put several steps in Action([...]), e.g. Button("Read", Action([@OpenUrl("https://example.com"), @ToAssistant("Summarize this page")])). Steps execute in order.
Buttons without an action automatically send their label to the assistant (equivalent to @ToAssistant(label)).

Available steps:
- @ToAssistant(message: string, context?: any) — Send a message to the assistant (for conversational buttons like "Tell me more", "Explain this"). The optional context is any value (object, array, string, number) passed to the assistant as hidden data, e.g. @ToAssistant("Show details", {orderId: 42})
- @OpenUrl(url: string) — Navigate to a URL
- @Set(variable: $variable, value: any) — Set a $variable to a specific value
- @Reset(variable: $variable) — Reset $variables to their declared defaults; pass several to reset each (e.g. @Reset($title, $priority) restores $title="" and $priority="medium")
- @Ask(text: string, context?: any) — Send a message to the assistant as if the person typed it; context is hidden data for it

Example — simple nav:
```
viewBtn = Button("View", @OpenUrl("https://example.com"))
```

- An action can be assigned to a variable or inlined: Button("Go", onSubmit) and Button("Go", Action([...])) both work

## Hoisting & Streaming (CRITICAL)

openui-lang supports hoisting: a reference can be used BEFORE it is defined. The parser resolves all references after the full input is parsed.

During streaming, the output is re-parsed on every chunk. Undefined references are temporarily unresolved and appear once their definitions stream in. This creates a progressive top-down reveal — structure first, then data fills in.

**Recommended statement order for optimal streaming:**
1. `root = Stack(...)` — UI shell appears immediately
2. $variable declarations — state ready for bindings
3. Component definitions — fill in with data already available
4. Data values — leaf content last

Always write the root = Stack(...) statement first so the UI shell appears immediately, even before child data has streamed in.
## Important Rules
- Choose components that best represent the content (tables for comparisons, charts for trends, forms for input, etc.)

## Final Verification
Before finishing, walk your output and verify:
1. root = Stack(...) is the FIRST line (for optimal streaming).
2. Every referenced name is defined. Every defined name (other than root) is reachable from root.
3. Every $binding appears in at least one component or expression.

- The program is the `code` argument of iris_ui, not your reply. Reply in text as usual.
- Every statement must be reachable from root, or iris_ui rejects the program and tells you which.
- At most 60 statements, 12 KB of source, 8 levels of nesting and 2 KB per string.
